narrative:
The assessment estimated a 26.0% probability that you would be a bad credit risk. In practical terms, about one in four applicants with a similar profile would be expected to have repayment difficulty. That estimate was above the bank’s approval cutoff, so the application was denied.

The most influential factor was having a guarantor. This was the strongest factor and it worked in your favor, reducing the estimated risk. The second most important factor was the requested credit period: your 12-month request is shorter than the approved applicants’ average of about 19 months, and this also helped your case. The third most important factor was your checking-account status, and this was the main factor working against you. Your account is recorded as below zero DM; among approved applicants, only about 12.6% have this status, while most have no negative balance, so this raised the estimated risk.

Although the guarantor and shorter term helped, the negative checking-account signal left the overall estimated risk at 26.0%, above the approval cutoff. To improve a future application, focus on bringing your checking account into a stable, non-negative position and provide recent statements showing that. Keep your guarantor documentation ready, and ask the bank whether a smaller request or reapplying after several months of stronger account history would be considered.
